statement: A DWN message is a signed operation description; a Record is logical state derived from accepted retained messages.
The initial RecordsWrite establishes Record identity and immutable fields that later updates must preserve.
Duplicate delivery of the same signed message must be idempotent with respect to logical Record state.
The final logical state of a Record must not depend on network delivery order when replicas possess the same valid message set.
In the current Enbox convergence model, a terminal delete dominates stale competing writes and prevents resurrection regardless of delivery order.
Retained message history and latest visible Record state are distinct projections and must not be conflated.
A state transition that changes latest logical Record state and its durable replication visibility must not leave a crash-observable split-brain between those projections.

Read-time $recordLimit occupancy is deterministic per exact protocol path and direct-parent context: each group ranks current latest live Records by dateCreated ascending then recordId ascending and admits the first max before caller filters, sort, and pagination. This is current Enbox behaviour, not the draft's admission-time reject/purgeOldest strategy.

RecordsRead, RecordsQuery, RecordsCount, and RecordsSubscribe snapshots resolve equivalent inputs to the same logical Record-ID population at the same durable head; Count counts that projected population.
